Build Quality & Materials

The Magnetic Wooden Chess Set is crafted from real walnut and maple. The contrast between the light and dark squares is clean and natural — no printed vinyl or painted veneer. The surrounding border has a smooth lacquered finish with brass hinges that feel solid when you fold and unfold the board. The closure snaps line up perfectly and keep the board shut during travel. The pieces are hand-carved in traditional Staunton style with a smooth, polished surface that looks and feels like a set that costs twice as much.

The WEgames Folding Set also uses real wood construction, though the finish is slightly less refined. The board surface is lacquered but the edges can feel a little sharp if you run a finger along them. The hinges are metal but not brass, and the folding mechanism works fine but doesn't feel quite as premium. The pieces are weighted with metal discs inside the base, giving them a satisfying heft that prevents easy toppling. They're not magnetic, but the weight keeps them reasonably stable for home play.

Material Note: Both sets use real wood (not plastic), but the Magnetic Chess Set uses walnut and maple specifically — two classic hardwoods that age beautifully. The WEgames set uses a lighter wood with a stained finish, which is still good but doesn't have the same depth of grain.

Magnetism: The Deciding Factor

Here's where these two sets diverge. The Magnetic Wooden Chess Set has magnets embedded in the base of every piece. The pull is strong enough that you can tilt the board to about 45 degrees before the pieces even think about shifting. On a train, in a car, on a wobbly cafe table — your setup stays put. The king has the strongest magnet since it's the tallest piece, and the pawns have just enough to stay planted without making it hard to slide them forward. It strikes a careful balance: the pieces stay during movement but lift cleanly when you make a move.

The WEgames set has no magnets. The pieces rely entirely on their weighted bases and felt bottoms. This works fine for table play — you're not going to knock them over easily — but one bump to the table or a slightly angled surface and you'll be picking up pieces. If you plan to play on the go, this is a meaningful difference.

The bottom line on magnets: If you'll only play at home on a flat table, the WEgames set is perfectly fine. If you plan to take your chess to a coffee shop, a park, a campsite, or an airplane — the magnetic version is the one that won't frustrate you.

Storage & Portability

Both boards fold in half and latch closed with metal snaps. But how they store the pieces inside is very different.

The Magnetic Wooden Chess Set uses custom foam inserts with cutouts for each piece. Every pawn, rook, knight, bishop, queen, and king has its own slot. This means zero rattling during travel — the foam holds everything snug. It also comes with two spare queens for pawn promotion, which are stored in their own slots. When you fold it up and snap it shut, the whole set is a compact 15" x 7.5" x 2" package that's easy to throw in a backpack or carry by the built-in handle.

The WEgames stores pieces in the board cavity, but they're loose — there's no foam or individual compartments. The pieces rattle around inside, which can be a minor annoyance. On the plus side, the board has a felt lining on the interior to prevent scratches, and the cavity is deep enough that everything stays inside when latched. It also includes an extra set of checkers pieces (since the board is reversible), which is a nice bonus.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are the magnets strong enough for travel?

Yes. The magnets hold pieces securely even when the board is tilted up to 45 degrees. They won't shift during normal travel — car rides, train trips, even light turbulence on a plane. The pieces lift cleanly when you pick them up to make a move.

Can the magnetic set be used for tournament play?

The board is regulation-friendly at 15" with 1.61" squares, but tournament play typically requires specific FIDE standards. For casual club play and home tournaments, it's perfectly suitable. The Staunton-style pieces are tournament-standard in design.

Does the WEgames set come with checkers pieces?

Yes. The reversible board has a checkerboard on the reverse side, and the set includes 24 checkers pieces (12 red, 12 black). This makes it a 2-in-1 value if you enjoy both games.

Do the pieces scratch the board?

Both sets have felt bottoms on every piece, so they slide smoothly without scratching the playing surface. With the Magnetic Wooden Chess Set, the foam storage also prevents pieces from rattling against each other during transport.

What if I lose a piece?

The Magnetic Wooden Chess Set includes two extra queens, which is great since the queen is the piece most commonly misplaced. For other pieces, the foam storage makes it immediately obvious if something is missing — no more wondering if you left a bishop at the cafe.

Final Thoughts

Chess is a game that rewards quality. A flimsy board with lightweight pieces that slide around doesn't just look cheap — it changes how you play. The Magnetic Wooden Chess Set eliminates that friction entirely. The pieces stay where you put them, the foam storage keeps everything organized, and the walnut-and-maple construction means this set will still look good on your coffee table years from now.

If you're on a tight budget, the WEgames set is a respectable option for home use. But spending the extra $11 on the Magnetic Wooden Chess Set buys you magnets that actually work, premium materials, and the peace of mind that your game won't fall apart when you take it on the road. For us, that's an easy call.
